paragraphs.text: Kisvei Beis Ishbitz–Radzin Parallel — Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 4:2: “Why was the Exodus from Egypt accompanied by haste (chipazon), as written: ‘You shall eat it in haste’ (Exodus 12:11) and ‘In haste you went forth from the land of Egypt’ (Deuteronomy 16:3), whereas of the future redemption it is said: ‘For you shall not go forth in haste’ (Isaiah 52:12)? At the Exodus from Egypt, Israel’s outer garments of body and nature were not yet fully refined, so the supernal light had to rescue them abruptly before the appointed time; in the future redemption, every vessel will be completely purified to receive the light in tranquil permanence.” Connection to this note: This Beis Ishbitz–Radzin teaching in Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 4:2 clarifies the inner dimension of Sotah 10b and directly illuminates Rav Tzadok's point in Divrei Chalomot 15.
